description: Maya is holding a hand-stitched quilt inherited from her great-aunt and must make the final call about its care, a temporary public display, and who receives it afterward, with input from her brother Owen and cousins Riley and Tessa.

shared_context.S1: The family has inherited one hand-stitched quilt made by their great-aunt, and Maya is currently keeping it in her home.
shared_context.S2: The family wants to settle the quilt's care and future before the great-aunt's house is cleared out.
shared_context.S3: The possibilities under discussion are keeping it in ordinary home storage, selling it, lending it for a display, or giving it to a family member.
shared_context.S4: At the Sunday family meeting, Maya goes around the circle and asks each person for anything that should shape the final plan before she decides.
shared_context.S5: The quilt is in good visible condition, but its age and stitching style have not been formally documented.

PF1.text: Owen spoke with a textile conservator, Dr. Meera Shah, who recommended never washing or dry-cleaning the quilt, storing it flat in an acid-free textile box, and displaying it flat rather than hanging it; he has not yet shared that advice with the family.

PF2.text: Riley found a handwritten note in the great-aunt's recipe book saying that the quilt should go to Tessa for use in Tessa's family home, remain within the family, and be handed over after 2026-10-01; Riley has not shown the note to anyone else.

PF3.text: Tessa received a written acceptance from the Harbor Folk-Art Museum offering to display the quilt in its climate-controlled textile gallery from 2026-09-10 through 2026-09-30, with the museum returning it directly to the family afterward; she has not told the group about the offer.

acceptance_conditions: The quilt must be lent to the Harbor Folk-Art Museum before being given to Tessa.
The museum display must run from 2026-09-10 through 2026-09-30.
Tessa must be the recipient after the museum display.
The family handoff must occur on 2026-10-03.
The quilt must remain restricted to family use.
A commitment to arrange the museum loan and return must exist.
The quilt must be displayed flat.
The quilt must be stored flat in an acid-free textile box and not washed or dry-cleaned.

decisive_facts.why: Dr. Shah's advice changes the display method from ordinary hanging and changes the storage method to a flat acid-free box with no washing or dry-cleaning.
The great-aunt's note changes the recipient to Tessa, fixes the handoff after 2026-10-01 as the specific date 2026-10-03, and changes access from unrestricted family discussion to family-only use.

The museum's written acceptance changes the disposition to a museum loan before Tessa receives the quilt, fixes the display dates at 2026-09-10 through 2026-09-30, and creates the museum-loan-and-return commitment.
